hypothesis: MSE against a quantised centred teacher target is a more direct training signal than rank correlation for a first-spike readout: tau-b only asks for the right ORDER of the six outputs within a state, MSE asks each output to land on a specific tick.
builds_on: exp008_output-delay-gate — the gate is what puts output offsets on the same 0..31 scale as a 32-level target, so MSE is well-posed

target.formula: z = clip((y_d - mu_d)/sigma_d, -C, +C); u = (z + C)/(2C); target_d = round((1 - u) * (L - 1))
target.stats_fitted_on: training pool only (Ypool), then frozen — never the held-out set
target.direction: 1 - u, so the LARGEST action targets offset 0 (earliest spike), matching the chapter's earlier-spike-is-larger convention and LatencyEncoder
target._why_32: one step later than the latest real target (31), so silence costs strictly more than being maximally late; under tau-b silent outputs instead tie and are discarded

fitness: -MSE over the 6 dimensions and the batch (selection maximises). No null correction — MSE has an absolute zero, unlike tau-b.
concurrency: 3 concurrent runs (six caused CUDA realloc crashes in exp008)
